title: Deferred Rendering Pipeline with G-Buffer Inspector and Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing a deferred rendering pipeline with a G-Buffer inspector using Three.js (via CDN). The scene must include:

## Scene Setup
- A perspective camera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin
- 5 objects: a red metallic sphere (roughness 0.2), a blue matte cube (roughness 0.9), a green glossy torus (roughness 0.3), a yellow cylinder (roughness 0.5), and a white plane floor (roughness 0.7)
- 3 point lights: warm light at (5,5,5) intensity 2.0, cool light at (-5,3,-3) intensity 1.5, fill light at (0,8,0) intensity 1.0
- Use MeshStandardMaterial for all objects
- Render to multiple render targets (MRT) simulating a G-Buffer with: albedo, normals (world space), depth, roughness/metalness channels

## G-Buffer Implementation
- Use WebGLRenderTarget with 4 texture attachments (or 4 separate render targets if MRT not available)
- Channel 0: Albedo (RGB color)
- Channel 1: World-space normals (encoded as RGB)
- Channel 2: Linear depth (grayscale, normalized 0-1 from near to far plane)
- Channel 3: Roughness (R channel) and Metalness (G channel)
- Use custom ShaderMaterial for the G-Buffer pass
- Use a fullscreen quad with a deferred lighting shader for the final composite

## G-Buffer Inspector UI
- A row of 5 buttons at the top: 'Composite', 'Albedo', 'Normals', 'Depth', 'Roughness/Metal'
- Clicking a button displays that buffer fullscreen on the canvas
- Active button gets a highlighted border (2px solid #00ff00)
- Current view mode stored in state

## Object Selection & Property Editing
- Click on objects in the 3D viewport to select them (use raycasting)
- Selected object gets a wireframe overlay
- A side panel (right side, 200px wide) shows selected object properties: name, color (hex input), roughness (slider 0-1), metalness (slider 0-1)
- Changing any property updates the object material AND re-renders the G-Buffer

## Undo/Redo System
- Maintain a history stack of property changes
- Ctrl+Z: undo last property change
- Ctrl+Y: redo last undone change
- History stores: {objectName, property, oldValue, newValue}
- Maximum history depth: 50 entries
- Display undo/redo count in a small HUD element (top-right corner)

## Light Controls
- Press keys 1, 2, 3 to toggle each point light on/off
- Press +/- to increase/decrease intensity of all active lights by 0.25
- Light state changes are also undoable

## Camera Controls
- OrbitControls for camera rotation/zoom
- Press 'R' to reset camera to initial position

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- viewMode: string ('composite'|'albedo'|'normals'|'depth'|'roughness_metal')
- selectedObject: string|null (name of selected object)
- objects: {name: {color: hex_string, roughness: number, metalness: number}} for all 5 objects
- lights: [{active: bool, intensity: number, position: [x,y,z]}, ...] for 3 lights
- historyIndex: number (current position in history stack)
- historyLength: number (total entries in history)
- canUndo: boolean
- canRedo: boolean
- lastAction: string (description of last action performed)
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z}
- gbufferResolution: {width, height}
- frameCount: number (increments each render)
- totalLightIntensity: number (sum of all active light intensities)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame and after every interaction.
physics_constraints: Light intensity must remain in range [0, 10]. Roughness and metalness must be clamped to [0, 1]. Total light intensity is the sum of intensities of active lights only. Camera position must be finite (no NaN). History index must satisfy: 0 <= historyIndex <= historyLength. Undo must exactly restore previous values. Depth buffer values must be normalized [0, 1].
